title: Floquet Engineering of Momentum Gaps in Magnonic Time Crystals: Slow-Drive Amplification and In-Gap Propagation
abstract: Photonic time crystals host momentum gaps in which waves grow exponentially but cannot propagate. We establish their magnonic counterpart in a thin film with periodically switched anisotropy, deriving its Floquet band structure and confirming it micromagnetically. Gaps require a precession-ellipticity contrast. The waveform controls high-order gaps: a single 1~GHz switching drive amplifies a comb of spin-wave bands, from 2.5 to 4.5~GHz, above Gilbert losses even with smoothed edges, unlike sinusoidal modulation. With the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction, amplified packets propagate inside the gap while growing.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to engineer momentum gaps in magnonic systems using time-periodic modulation of magnetic anisotropy. It shows that a slow drive can amplify multiple spin-wave bands within these gaps, and critically, that the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction enables these amplified wave packets to propagate stably inside the gap structure.
main_problem: To establish and analyze the magnonic counterpart of photonic time crystals, specifically investigating how momentum gaps (MGs) are engineered using Floquet theory in a system with periodically switched anisotropy.
main_result: The study demonstrates that a slow, periodic drive can amplify multiple spin-wave bands above intrinsic losses, and the inclusion of Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction allows these amplified wave packets to propagate rigidly inside the momentum gap.
method: The analysis relies on deriving the Floquet band structure using the monodromy matrix approach applied to the linearized Landau–Lifshitz equation, which is then compared against micromagnetic simulations.
model_or_system: The system is an ultrathin ferromagnetic film with periodically switched perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), modeled by the linearized Landau–Lifshitz equation. The dynamics are governed by the temporal modulation of the PMA, $Q(t)$.
key_observables: Floquet band structure (Real and Imaginary parts of the quasi-frequency $f_F$ vs $k$), amplification rate ($	ext{Im } f_F$), and the induced drift velocity ($v_D$).
important_parameters: The modulation frequency ($f_{	ext{mod}}$), the bias field ($B_0$), and the strength of the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the linearized Landau–Lifshitz equation and assumes the system can be described by a two-state protocol for calculating the monodromy matrix.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of the anisotropy, the resulting Floquet band structure showing gaps, and wave dynamics both inside and outside the gaps under different modulation waveforms and DMI effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework using Floquet theory and the monodromy matrix to predict gap opening. It then details the role of the modulation waveform in controlling higher-order gaps and demonstrates slow-drive amplification. Finally, it incorporates DMI to show gap-protected wave propagation.
why_interesting: This work applies advanced concepts from Floquet engineering and parametric amplification, which are highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics, by translating them into the realm of magnonics.

Figure 2 follows the dynamics at the two wave vectors marked in Fig. 1(b), outside (k = 4 rad/µm) and in- side (k = 24 rad/µm) the first MG. Outside the gap, the modulation generates a time-reflected component, visi- ble in the spectra as a negative-frequency peak (reversed phase velocity), but the amplitudes remain bounded [Fig. 2(a,c,e)]. Inside the gap, the forward and back- ward components grow exponentially to comparable am- plitudes and form a standing wave [Fig. 2(b,d), inset], analogous to photonic time crystals [14].
